en.headline: Court dismisses Zen and four others’ appeal over 612 fund
en.dek: The Court of Appeal rejected challenges by Cardinal Joseph Zen and four co-trustees against their 2022 convictions for failing to register the 612 Humanitarian Relief Fund.
body: A Hong Kong court on Thursday dismissed appeals brought by Cardinal Joseph Zen and four others against their convictions for failing to register a fund that assisted people arrested during the 2019 protests.

Zen, the 94-year-old retired bishop of Hong Kong, was a trustee of the 612 Humanitarian Relief Fund together with singer Denise Ho, scholar Hui Po-keung, and former legislators Margaret Ng and Cyd Ho. The fund provided medical and legal support until it ceased operations in October 2021.

The five were found guilty in 2022 of breaching the Societies Ordinance by not registering the organisation or seeking an exemption within a month of its establishment. Each was fined HK$4,000. Their convictions were the first under that provision of the ordinance.
The appeal focused on whether the fund met the statutory definition of a society. The Court of Appeal upheld the original findings.

zh.headline: 陳日君等五人612基金案上訴遭駁回
zh.dek: 高等法院上訴庭周四駁回樞機主教陳日君及另外四名信託人就2022年未有登記612人道支援基金定罪的上訴。
body: 高等法院上訴庭周四駁回樞機主教陳日君及另外四名信託人就未有登記612人道支援基金定罪的上訴。
陳日君與歌手何韻詩、學者許寶強、前立法會議員吳靄儀及何秀蘭同為612人道支援基金信託人。該基金在2019年反修例事件期間為被捕人士提供醫療及法律支援，直至2021年10月停止運作。
五人於2022年被裁定違反《社團條例》，未有在基金成立後一個月內登記或申請豁免，各被判罰款4,000港元。該案是條例相關條文下的首宗定罪。
上訴主要圍繞基金是否符合法例對「社團」的定義。上訴庭維持原審裁決。
